title: Graceful Degradation Routing / Lane Design (WIP)
content:
Context and goal:

Quick working notes on a lane-based admission + graceful degradation approach for capacity-aware routing across regions and GPU pools. The aim is to keep latency SLOs for high-priority traffic while maximizing utilization and avoiding hard rejects when capacity shifts (region failovers, noisy-neighbor spikes, degraded hardware). This is intentionally informal — experiments + TODOs below.

Key ideas (high level):
- Lanes: allocate requests into dynamic lanes (hot, warm, cold, background) by priority, tenant SLAs, and cost-sensitivity. Lanes are logical admission classes not physical queues.
- Soft-throttle + partial responses: instead of immediate 429s when a lane saturates, apply progressive degradation: reduce max tokens, enable early stop sequences, route to cheaper/quantized model variants, or enqueue with a bounded polite wait.
- Predictive headroom: each serving pool (region+pool) maintains a short-term forecast (30s–2min) of available tokens/sec and GPU load using EWMA + ML-lite predictor. Admission decisions consider predicted capacity, not just instantaneous metrics.
- Multi-region priority failover: maintain per-tenant preferred region list and cost/latency tiers; perform fast fallback when a preferred region loses headroom, routing to the next acceptable region with a graded degradation strategy (first try same model family, then quantized variant, then smaller model).
- Signals: admission uses token-bucket approximations for lane budgets, queue-depth signals for backpressure, and GPU-utilization + SM occupancy + power capping events. Combine into a single lane score.

High-level admission flow (sketch):
1) Request arrives at edge/plumbing (API gateway). Auth + tenant metadata retrieved.
2) Assign lane using ruleset: tenant SLA, request hint (interactive vs batch), cost flag, model family.
3) Query local control plane for lane budgets and pool headroom forecast.
4) Compute lane score: s = f(bucket_remaining, predicted_headroom, queue_depth_penalty, gpu_signal_penalty).
5) If s >= accept_threshold -> accept, assign to pool and deduct budget. If s in (soft_threshold, accept_threshold) -> soft-degrade (truncate, route to quantized variant, or enqueue with polite wait token). If s < soft_threshold -> degrade aggressively or reroute to fallback region.

Design elements to call out:
- Token-bucket semantics per lane: we keep a per-lane token budget that refills at a rate derived from SLO throughput targets. Tokens represent "capacity units" where 1 unit approximates 1k tokens output or X ms GPU time. We need to standardize the unit.
- Queue depth vs latency headroom: don't use queue depth alone; map queue depth to expected added latency using observed p95/p99 profiles and incorporate that into scoring.
- GPU signals: direct GPU util (SM occupancy), model stage stalls, power cap events. Translate to "effective headroom multiplier" (0..1).
- Predictive model: light-weight AR(1)/linear EWMA on recent token consumption + hour-of-day multiplier + outlier detection. ML model can be added later for seasonalities.

Admission policy examples:
- System-critical tenant (SLA gold): accept_threshold low, smaller soft-degradation window. We prefer model variant fallback over truncation.
- Consumer tenant (free tier): larger soft-degrade range, prefer token-limited responses and queuing credit.
- Background batch: accept only if pool headroom > 40% and token budget available, otherwise defer to scheduled windows.

Routing & multi-region failover rules:
- Primary route preferred_region -> local pool. If predicted headroom < 10% for 15s -> begin staged failover:
  * Stage 1 (fast): route new requests to next region but mark for soft-degrade (shorter max tokens). Keep a small fraction (~5%) to primary to probe recovery.
  * Stage 2 (moderate): reduce concurrency in primary pool via brief token reweighting, force quantized variants.
  * Stage 3 (recover): when primary forecast recovers for 30s, ramp back using canary percentage increases.
- Cost-aware routing: route to cheaper region if latency increase < SLO slack and cost delta > threshold. Useful for non-latency-sensitive requests.

Observability and metrics to track (minimum):
- per-lane: tokens_consumed, tokens_refilled, accept_rate, soft_degrade_rate, reject_rate, avg_latency, p95_latency, fallback_rate_to_region_X
- per-pool: predicted_headroom, gpu_sm_occupancy, power_cap_events, queue_depth, in_flight_requests
- control-plane: decisions/sec, avg scoring latency, versioned policy snapshot id

Experimentation plan (short):
- Experiment A: soft-throttle vs hard 429 on spikes (pilot: 2 weeks, dev-stage region). Metrics: user-visible p95 latency, total tokens saved, fallback incidents, customer error rate.
- Experiment B: predictive headroom ON vs OFF. Measure false positives (rejects when not necessary) and false negatives (missed overloads).
- Experiment C: lane-weighted token units (GPU-time approximated) vs simple per-token units. Compare headroom accuracy and scheduling fairness.

Open questions / risks (notes):
- Unit definition: tokens vs GPU-time vs combined "cost units". We need a canonical mapping per model variant. Action: create mapping doc and run calibration jobs for common models.
- Control plane latency: making per-request checks to control plane adds overhead. Need local caches with TTL and circuit-breakers.
- Fairness vs deterministic guarantees: danger of starvation for low-priority tenants during long outages. Consider long-term credit system so background jobs get scheduled eventually.
- Rapid oscillation when pools partially recover -> implement hysteresis and probe traffic fraction to avoid flip-flopping.

Implementation notes (practical):
- Keep admission scoring in edge-process that is <1ms path: precompute lane thresholds and use cached headroom. Heavy forecasting runs asynchronously.
- Use gRPC stream from pool agents to control-plane with 1s heartbeat for SM occupancy + queue depth + tail latency signals. Pool agents publish lightweight forecast every 5s.
- Persist lane budgets in control-plane Redis with per-lane tokens stored as integer tenths to avoid float drift.
- Policy rollout via console: support canary percentages, global default, tenant overrides. Policy snapshots must be versioned and traceable to decisions.

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Calibrate cost-unit mapping for 3 model families (gpt-like-13B, llama-2-70b, gpt-small). Owner: Maya. ETA: 2025-10-10.
- [ ] Implement pool agent heartbeat prototype. Owner: Noah. ETA: 2025-10-03.
- [ ] Wire conservative local cache for lane budgets in gateway (TTL 500ms) and benchmark added latency. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2025-09-26.
- [ ] Run Experiment A in dev-region for 2 weeks, gather metrics. Owner: Evelyn. ETA: start 2025-10-06.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally design-first; we should align on the cost-unit mapping before optimizations. I'm expecting tradeoffs here — please call out any hard requirements from SRE/infra on acceptable control-plane QPS or cache staleness.
